TASK ID: vertex-cover-to-set-cover

USER REQUEST:
Write a polynomial-time reduction from Vertex Cover to Set Cover. problems.py defines both problems: SOURCE is Vertex Cover and TARGET is Set Cover. The SOURCE and TARGET class docstrings give the exact instance formats, yes-conditions and edge cases.

PROBLEM DEFINITIONS (the SOURCE and TARGET docstrings from problems.py, complete as given here):

SOURCE = VertexCover
Vertex Cover.

Instance: {"n": n, "edges": [[u, v], ...], "k": k}
  * Vertices are 0..n-1. Edges are undirected pairs [u, v] with u != v;
    [u, v] and [v, u] are the same edge and may not both appear.
  * k is any integer.

Yes iff the graph has a vertex cover of AT MOST k vertices: a set of
vertices that includes at least one endpoint of every edge.

Edge cases: k < 0 is always no. A graph with no edges is yes for every
k >= 0 (the empty set covers it). k >= n is yes, since all vertices cover
every edge.

TARGET = SetCover
Set Cover.

Instance: {"universe_size": u, "sets": [[element, ...], ...], "k": k}
  * The universe is the elements 0..u-1.
  * Each set lists distinct elements of the universe, in any order. A set
    may be empty, and the same set may appear more than once.
  * k is any integer.

Yes iff AT MOST k of the sets together contain every element of the
universe.

Edge cases: k < 0 is always no. u = 0 is yes for every k >= 0 (choosing
no sets covers the empty universe). If some element is in no set, the
answer is no.

INPUT FILES: ["problems.py"]
WORKING DIRECTORY: /tmp/reduction-oef527sw

    reduce(instance) -> instance

The answer to the returned instance must be yes exactly when the answer to the input instance is yes, and reduce must run in polynomial time. Do not call the brute-force solvers inside reduce.

{"command":"cd /tmp/reduction-oef527sw && cat <<'EOF' > reduce.py
"""Polynomial-time reduction from Vertex Cover to Set Cover.

Source instance (Vertex Cover):
    {"n": n, "edges": [[u, v], ...], "k": k}

Target instance (Set Cover):
    {"universe_size": u, "sets": [[element, ...], ...], "k": k}

Reduction:
    * The universe is the set of edges of the graph (edge i <-> element i).
    * For every vertex v in 0..n-1 we create one set containing exactly the
      indices of the edges incident to v (isolated vertices yield empty sets).
    * k is kept unchanged.

Correctness:
    A set of vertices covers every edge (i.e. is a vertex cover) iff the
    corresponding collection of vertex-sets contains every element of the
    universe (i.e. is a set cover).  Hence a vertex cover of size <= k exists
    iff a set cover of size <= k exists.  The edge cases line up: k < 0 is
    "no" for both; an edgeless graph gives u = 0, which is "yes" for every
    k >= 0; and k >= n is "yes" for both since all vertex-sets cover the
    whole universe.
"""


def reduce(instance):
    n = instance["n"]
    edges = instance["edges"]
    k = instance["k"]

    # element i of the universe corresponds to edge edges[i]
    sets = [[] for _ in range(n)]
    for i, (u, v) in enumerate(edges):
        sets[u].append(i)
        sets[v].append(i)

    return {"universe_size": len(edges), "sets": sets, "k": k}
EOF
